name: Scourge
summary: The Scourge is an apocalyptic army of undead monsters, necromancers, and enslaved spirits bound to the will of the Lich King. Originally created by the Burning Legion to destabilize Azeroth ahead of the Third War, the legion of walking corpses broke free from demonic control and shattered the kingdoms of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas. Today, they wage unending war from their arctic stronghold in Northrend and their corrupt dominion over the Plaguelands.

sections.title: A Plague of Demonic Design
sections.body: The Scourge was born as an instrument of destruction forged by the Burning Legion. The demon lords bound the spirit of the fallen orc shaman Ner'zhul to the Frozen Throne in distant Northrend, fashioning him into the Lich King. With terrifying telepathic power, he was commanded to prepare Azeroth for conquest. The Lich King unleashed the Plague of Undeath southward into the unsuspecting human realm of Lordaeron, relying on the mortal traitors of the Cult of the Damned to poison grain supplies. Those who perished arose not as restful dead, but as twisted thralls entirely subservient to the Lich King's iron mind.

sections.title: The Fall of the North
sections.body: The Scourge achieved total devastation when Prince Arthas Menethil fell to the Lich King's whispers. Seeking vengeance in Northrend, Arthas claimed the cursed blade Frostmourne and forfeited his soul, becoming the Scourge's paramount death knight. Returning home, Arthas slew his father King Terenas, butchered Capital City, and unleashed the undead horde across Lordaeron. The Scourge swept through towns like Darrowshire and Andorhal, butchered the Silver Hand paladins, destroyed Dalaran to summon Archimonde, and carved a dead scar through Quel'Thalas to resurrect Kel'Thuzad as a lich.

sections.title: Betrayal and the Schism
sections.body: The Lich King never intended to serve the Burning Legion permanently. Through Arthas, Ner'zhul secretly engineered the Legion's defeat by goading Illidan Stormrage into slaying the dreadlord Tichondrius in Felwood. Enraged, the demon lord Kil'jaeden later ordered Illidan to obliterate the Frozen Throne. Illidan's assault fractured the icy prison, causing the Lich King's mental grip over his minions to waver. Seizing on this weakened control, a faction of free-willed undead led by the resurrected banshee Sylvanas Windrunner broke away, christened themselves the Forsaken, and seized the ruins of Lordaeron.

sections.title: The Present Threat
sections.body: Though weakened by the fracturing of the Frozen Throne and the rebellion of the Forsaken, the Scourge remains the deadliest force in the northern world. Led in the field by the lich Kel'Thuzad, its abominations, crypt fiends, and necromancers dominate the corrupted Eastweald and Westweald, now known as the Plaguelands. From grim bastions and blighted fields, they continuously wage war against the Forsaken of the Undercity, the fanatic zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, and the remaining enclaves of the Alliance.

faq.answer: The Scourge is a vast empire of undead thralls, necromancers, and warped beasts bound mentally to the Lich King. They exist solely to destroy all living things and convert the corpses of the fallen into obedient servants.

The Scourge is commanded by the Lich King from his Frozen Throne in the distant, icy continent of Northrend. In the ruined lands of Lordaeron, his armies are directed locally by powerful lieutenants such as the lich Kel'Thuzad and the death knight Arthas Menethil.

faq.q: How does the Scourge differ from the Forsaken?
aliases: why are undead fighting each other
faq.answer: The Scourge are mindless or dominated undead enslaved to the psychic will of the Lich King. The Forsaken are former Scourge victims who regained their free will when the Lich King's power weakened. Led by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Forsaken despise the Scourge and fight fiercely to annihilate them.

faq.q: Why did the Scourge attack Lordaeron?
faq.answer: The Burning Legion ordered the Lich King to spread the Plague of Undeath across Lordaeron to slaughter its people, weaken the Alliance, and clear away any resistance before the demons began their invasion of Azeroth during the Third War.

faq.q: Who is the Cult of the Damned?
faq.answer: The Cult of the Damned is a mortal organization founded by the archmage Kel'Thuzad. Its members are living humans who willingly serve the Lich King, lured by promises of dark magical power and eternal life through undeath. They were responsible for spreading the tainted grain that initiated the plague.

faq.q: How was Prince Arthas corrupted by the Scourge?
aliases: why did arthas betray his people
faq.answer: Driven to obsession while trying to save his kingdom from the plague, Prince Arthas pursued the dreadlord Mal'Ganis to Northrend. In desperation, Arthas took up the cursed runeblade Frostmourne, which stole his soul. Broken and twisted by the Lich King's whispers, he returned as the Scourge's premier champion and butchered his own homeland.

angles.text: Every Forsaken was once an enslaved instrument of the Scourge, forced to butcher friends and kin until the Lich King's grip slipped. Eradicating the Scourge is not just a war of survival; it is a campaign of absolute personal vengeance.
The Scourge destroyed humanity's greatest kingdom, slaughtered the line of Menethil, and transformed the heartland of Lordaeron into a blighted wasteland.

The Knights of the Silver Hand were shattered by the Scourge when Prince Arthas turned on his own mentors and murdered Uther the Lightbringer. For any paladin, cleansing the Scourge with the Holy Light is a sacred duty.
The memory of Lordaeron's fall remains an open wound for the Alliance, driving their ongoing military efforts to reclaim the Plaguelands and avenge the fallen.
With the Forsaken now accepted into the Horde, the entire coalition finds itself drawn into the brutal, ongoing war against the remnants of the Lich King's armies in the north.
